Formulation
Predisposing: History of eczema.  
Precipitating: Unknown trigger; potential contact irritant not yet identified.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing itch–scratch cycle disrupting sleep and concentration.  
Protective: Employed, living with others, willing to seek medical help.

Mental Health Care Plan Details
(No explicit mental health conditions identified; plan focuses on sleep disturbance secondary to dermatological flare.)

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Obtain relief from itching to restore normal sleep and daily functioning.
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce pruritus and skin inflammation; monitor impact on sleep and mood.
- Actions (Patient):
  • Use prescribed topical steroid and emollient regimen for 7–10 days.  
  • Trial stronger antihistamine (Fexofenadine as prescribed).  
  • Keep diary of possible triggers (soaps, detergents, fabrics).  
  • Return for review if no improvement within one week.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Prescribe potent topical steroid, emollient, and non-sedating antihistamine.  
  • Provide instructions on application and skin care.  
  • Arrange follow-up review in one week; assess sleep and mental well-being.  
  • Consider dermatology referral if inadequate response.

Secondary Problem: Not recorded

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Use of topical steroids/emollients, antihistamine options, trigger identification.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased itch, spread of rash, further sleep disruption.
- Coping Strategies: Regular emollient use, cool showers, avoid known irritants, maintain trigger diary.
